jobs.title: Sr Technical Product Manager
jobs.description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

The Terrestrial Software team is building the foundation for an automated rocket factory and integrated launch platform. Their mission is to automate and streamline workflows across the entire lifecycle of Terran R, from raw material intake to launch operations and eventually manufacturing on Mars. Today, that means partnering directly with teams across design, materials, manufacturing, and test and launch to design, implement, and deploy enduser enterprise-wide applications, industrial automation, data analytics infrastructure, and next-generation AI to solve real problems and accelerate progress. Long term, the team is laying the groundwork for a modular, scalable software platform that can power highly autonomous operations on Earth and beyond. This is a team for builders and thinkers who thrive on cross-functional impact and want to shape the digital backbone of our future in space.

About the Role:

You will be responsible for designing, building, and continuously evolving scalable process infrastructure across the factory and supply chain ecosystem. You will take end-to-end ownership of core enterprise workflows—including MRP, procure-to-pay, material conveyance, factory automation, and change management—treating each as a product with a lifecycle that demands constant improvement, stakeholder alignment, and technical rigor. This role blends systems engineering, process design, and software integration, requiring both a deep understanding of manufacturing and supply chain operations and the ability to design technical solutions that are robust, intuitive, and performance-driven.

- Architect and own end-to-end enterprise workflows across planning and execution, MRP, procure-to-pay, material movement, and change control—ensuring alignment with business needs and scalable technical solutions

- Develop and maintain technical infrastructure that supports process-as-a-product workflows, with a focus on data integrity, reliability, automation, and integration with enterprise systems. Continuously monitor and optimize performance across key workflows—leveraging real-time data to drive improvements in scheduling accuracy, fulfillment velocity, inventory health, and process compliance

- Collaborate cross-functionally with manufacturing, supply chain, software engineering, finance, and operations teams to define requirements, implement process changes, and deliver high-impact systems that drive efficiency and agility. Partner with product managers, analysts, and business stakeholders to translate complex operational needs into scalable, elegant solutions that create measurable value across the organization

- Lead factory and supply chain automation initiatives by identifying opportunities for digital transformation, designing integrated workflows, and ensuring seamless orchestration between physical and digital systems and establish and enforce rigorous standards for change management and data governance across the enterprise, ensuring consistency, traceability, and operational reliability. Deliver and maintain high-quality documentation of technical architecture, process flows, and interface contracts to support transparency, scalability, and team alignment

- A talent for distilling complex technical concepts into clear, concise explanations for non-experts.

About You:

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Supply Chain/Operations Management, or a related discipline

- 3+ years of working in a supply chain engineering, product engineering, software engineering  or product management role with a focus on MRP or ERP systems within an advanced manufacturing environment

- Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, SQL, Javascript, Java, C#

- Advanced knowledge of supply chain and/or manufacturing processes

- Strong working knowledge of at least one of the following enterprise processes/workflows:

- Enterprise Planning / Material Requirements Planning for advanced manufacturing

- Procure to Pay

- Material Conveyance / Material Flow Automation

- Change Management / Config Management

- Manufacturing Execution / Factory Automation

- Data Integrity / Data Governance

Nice to haves but not required:

- Strong understanding of a variety of codebased technical infrastructure and information systems / database architecture

- Experience with cloud platforms and distributed systems

- Familiarity with modern software development practices and tools, including version control, continuous integration, and automated testing

At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors.

Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here.

Hiring Range:
$129,000 — $193,000 USD

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

About the Team:

The Vehicle Engineering organization at Relativity Space owns the Terran R launch vehicle across its full life cycle - from design through build, qualification, and flight - along with the analysis, software, CONOPs development, risk management, and customer-facing and regulatory activities needed to operate Terran R successfully.

About the Role:

- We are seeking a Staff Technical Program Manager to manage cross-functional program execution across a product lifecycle from early design through to flight. We are looking for someone who is comfortable operating between the 10,000 ft. view of the program and zooming in to solve a critical bottleneck. In this role, they will collaborate with technical leaders, manufacturing and ops counterparts, and other program managers to ensure successful execution of top line business objectives, often translating ambiguous long-term ideas into a set of clear trade-offs and priorities. They will analyze problems and drive recommendations that balance the needs of technical teams and the business, anchoring back to data. They will actively own and manage schedules, identify & mitigate programmatic risk, and drive communication across functional teams. A strong desire to build agile, fit for purpose processes from scratch, get your hands dirty, and influence a wide range of technical and operational teams are foundational to success in this role.

Execution Strategy & Risk Management

- Translate long-term business objectives and priorities into a clear execution plan for your area of ownership

- Build and own the schedule, deriving it from real requirements, resources, and dependencies & ensuring alignment with key company milestones

- Identify, assess, and mitigate risks associated with program execution, ensuring proactive resolution of issues coming down the pipeline

- Identify resource gaps and coordinate cross-functional planning for resource allocation, including headcount, budget, and workspace needs

- Develop ways of working and cadences between teams to ensure efficient execution, collaboration, and alignment

- Communicate program updates, risks, and trade-offs to senior management and cross-functional stakeholders, grounded in data, deciphering signal from noise, and driving decision making when required

- Identify and drive to resolve future programmatic risks, keeping line of sight to 12mo+ strategic initiatives that are critical for business milestones

Cross-Functional and Strategic Leadership

- Collaborate with PMOs and department leaders to integrate workstream schedules into the program-level Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), and use the IMS to understand true program critical path, dependencies, and decision points

- Work with functional partners to align priorities when there are competing needs. Drive improvements to department-level program management tooling to continually improve program efficiency and operational excellence

- Coordinate efforts across key bodies of work over development lifecycle, including design release, engineering trades, handoffs between teams, and operational burndown ahead of key milestones. Incorporate new capabilities leveraging automation and AI, when available

- Lead by influence and collaborate with technical owners (engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, test, and launch) to establish a plan & empower strong functional ownership

Process Improvement & Team Growth

- Spearhead the creation and continual refinement of effective, lightweight program management processes, tools, and templates that improve efficiency and cross-team collaboration

- Establish ways of working and ownership model to that ensure programmatic lessons learned are being incorporated each design, build, test, launch cycle

- Build trust, credibility, and buy-in with functional team & program stakeholders to implement processes effectively

Goal Tracking & Reporting

- Establish goals and metrics to monitor program performance and increase the predictability and efficiency of engineering work

- Monitor and report on progress toward organizational goals, objectives, and milestones, presenting an objective and clear path forward

- Facilitate strong communication within departments and across the program to ensure transparency in program status & maintain culture of high ownership

About You:

- Bachelor's degree in engineering, science, mathematics, or a related field; aerospace, electrical, or mechanical engineering degree preferred

- 7+ years leading a complex program. This can include work in a program management role or a technical role where you were leading a large
complex technical hardware program. Experience spanning software and operations preferred

- Demonstrated success supporting cross-functional hardware teams from concept through delivery in fast-paced, high-ambiguity environments
Able to move fluidly between tactical execution and big-picture perspective

- Track record of solving ambiguous problems, developing processes and tools from scratch. Able to work scrappy whilst building sustainable longterm
processes

- Proven ability to communicate with highly technical teams and bridge communication between technical and non-technical audiences

- A systems mindset: able to identify program dependencies, interfaces, and risks, and understand the impact of technical and program decisions
on other teams and at the company level

Nice to haves but not required:

- Hands-on experience with launch vehicles, propulsion systems, or aerospace hardware

- PMP, MBA, Master's in engineering, science, mathematics, or related field, or equivalent experience

- Strong executive presence, with the ability to drive clarity and action across all levels of the company

- Technical leadership experience, proven track record of success and strategic thinking while balancing conflicting priorities and goals

About the Team:

The Tooling and Factory Automation team sits at the intersection of design, manufacturing, and automation, making everything from large-scale structural fixtures to small tools that directly enable Terran R’s production. As a design group embedded within the manufacturing organization, we dig deep into the needs of our internal partners to understand root problems, propose solutions, and deliver hardware to help build faster, scale smarter, and work better. The team is also at the forefront of Relativity’s growing factory automation efforts, an increasingly critical part of scaling production of Terran R at existing and future facilities. You’ll have the autonomy to make decisions, field solutions, and see them in action on the factory floor. Ultimately, you’re not just delivering tools or automated processes; you’re defining how rockets and factories get built.

About the Role:

- Collaborate with leadership to forge a strategic growth roadmap for the Tooling and Factory Automation org that propels company-wide objectives and partnerships

- Create and facilitate team infrastructure in the form of frameworks, digital productivity tools, and physical resources

- Coordinate people, scope, timelines, interactions and communications to achieve the highest standards of team effectiveness and service to customers

- Contribute to innovation through direct engagement in design activities and definition of strategic technological initiatives

- Establish and track metrics that define the team’s impact

About You:

- Degree in engineering, science, mathematics, or related fields; mechanical, aerospace or electrical engineering degree preferred

- 5+ years in program or project management role(s)

- Experience managing multiple customers across matrix organizations and building sustainable processes

- Experience in the manufacturing of complex parts and assemblies

- Proven ability to solve challenging technical problems and develop robust, scalable solutions

Nice to haves but not required:

- •Experience in the development and integration of tooling and automated manufacturing equipment

- High volume manufacturing experience

Relativity Space pioneered large-scale additive manufacturing with our Terran 1 rocket, the largest 3D-printed object to fly. Now a distinct business unit within Relativity, Horizon Manufacturing Technologies is advancing next-generation manufacturing for aerospace and beyond. The team operates at the frontier of manufacturing innovation, where creativity meets capability. This is an environment where cutting-edge R&D is put into production, industrializing advanced manufacturing capabilities to solve customer problems. You’ll work alongside welders, robotics engineers, data scientists, and systems engineers at the intersection of hardware and software, creating an end-to-end additive manufacturing platform that serves a wide variety of applications. From exploring new materials to unlocking faster print speeds, to designing complex, organic geometries that can’t be built any other way, it’s high-impact work that sets the foundation for the future of advanced manufacturing.

- Lead complex programs from kickoff through delivery, partnering with engineering, operations, supply chain, and customers to execute against cost, schedule, and technical objectives.

- Translate customer requirements and program goals into actionable plans, driving alignment across cross-functional teams and maintaining visibility into progress, risks, and dependencies.

- Serve as the primary interface between technical teams, leadership, and customers, facilitating technical reviews, communicating program status, and enabling timely decision-making.

- Own program execution by maintaining integrated schedules, preparing customer-facing status reports, coordinating and reviewing technical deliverables, and ensuring clear, accurate communication throughout the program lifecycle

- Own the commercial and operational success of assigned programs, maintaining accountability for budgets, forecasts, customer commitments, contract execution, schedule performance and overall program profitability.

- Drive program governance by managing requirements, configuration and change control, risk mitigation, and compliance with quality and regulatory standards.

About You:

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Program Management, or a related technical field.

- 3+ years of experience managing multiple technical programs in aerospace, defense, advanced manufacturing, or another highly regulated engineering environment.

- Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence technical and business stakeholders without direct authority.

- Proven ability to influence technical decisions and align diverse stakeholders around common objectives.

- Exceptional technical writing and communication skills, with experience developing customer-facing reports, reviewing technical documentation, and translating complex engineering concepts into clear, actionable communication.

- Excellent commercial and financial awareness, with experience framing decisions in terms of cost, timing, risk and performance.

Nice to haves but not required:

- Experience with additive manufacturing, advanced manufacturing, or new product development.

- Working knowledge of quality and regulatory standards such as AS9100, ISO 9001, ITAR/EAR, DFARS, or NIST 800-171

- Project Management Professional Certification (PMP)

- Knowledge of materials, manufacturing, operations and additive manufacturing standards.
